title: Lab 234 - Network File System (NFS)
description: Manage an NFS client using three preconfigured NFS server shares with different access and root-mapping behaviors. Students will install and verify NFS client utilities, discover NFS exports, manually mount read-only and read-write NFS shares, demonstrate root_squash and no_root_squash behavior, configure persistent NFS mounts, and verify /etc/fstab configuration.

lab_objective.description: By the end of this lab, students should be able to:
objectives: Discover NFS exports from a server.
Understand the difference between ro and rw.
Demonstrate the security implications of root access from an NFS client.
Test file creation, modification, and deletion.
Use mount, findmnt, df, and /proc/mounts to troubleshoot NFS mounts.
Understand why client-side rw does not override a server-side ro export.

scenario: You are working as a Linux Systems Administrator responsible for managing NFS client systems in an organization.
The NFS server has already been configured and is providing three NFS exports to the client.
NFS Client: Your assigned Linux client VM

The three exports are configured with different access and root-mapping behaviors.

Your task is to manage the NFS client only, discover the available exports, mount each share, test read and write behavior, demonstrate the difference between root_squash and no_root_squash, and configure all three NFS mounts to persist using /etc/fstab.

completion_message: Excellent work! You have completed Lab 234 - Network File System (NFS). You practiced NFS client package management, NFS export discovery, manual NFS mounting, read-only and read-write access testing, root_squash and no_root_squash behavior, UID/GID ownership verification, and persistent NFS mounts using /etc/fstab.
